summary: Master wax-chandler of Dasà in Calabria and father of Giovanni Cognetta; John's maternal 3rd-great-grandfather.
bio: Nicola Cognetta was born at Dasà in Calabria about 1804, though some records say 1802, the son of Francesco Cognetta, born in 1771, and Domenica Malvaso (1781–1848). He married Mariantonia Cannatello, who was born about 1816 and whose name is also given as Mariangiola. He was a ceraiuolo, a wax-chandler who made votive and church candles, and was styled 'Mastro', a title that marked an artisan of slightly elevated standing. When his son Giovanni was born at Dasà on 22 March 1855, Nicola was 51. He died at Dasà in 1878. He is John's maternal 3rd-great-grandfather, through a link between his son Giovanni and Frank that is probable rather than fully proven.

researchNotes: Tree: Nicola Cognetta (1802-1878) + Mariantonia Cannatello (b. 1816); parents Francesco Cognetta (b. 1771) + Domenica Malvaso (1781-1848). Round 1: a MyHeritage index entry (via search extract) shows Mariangiola Cognetta née Cannatello, born 1818 in Dasà, married to Nicola Cognetta - almost certainly the same couple. Round 3: in Giovanni's birth act (22 Mar 1855, Dasà, Nati 1855 act 18) he is 'Mastro Nicola Cognetta', 51 (b. c.1804, not 1802), ceraiuolo (wax-chandler / candle-maker, who made votive and church candles). 'Mastro' marks an artisan of slightly elevated status.
